claims.text: Applying a thin nanostructured W–Ta–Cr–V–Hf refractory HEA coating to tungsten particles will enhance interfacial thermal conduction in a W–Cu composite.
The HEA coating will not impair the mechanical durability of the W–Cu composite.
The HEA coating will preserve the irradiation resistance of the W–Cu composite.
Conventional tungsten–copper interfaces exhibit higher thermal boundary resistance than the proposed HEA-modified interfaces.
Coating tungsten particles before consolidation will produce a uniform HEA interlayer at the tungsten–copper interface.
The HEA interlayer will improve lattice and phonon matching between tungsten and copper.
The HEA interlayer will act as a sink for irradiation-induced defects.
A gradated transition in vibrational properties between tungsten and copper will reduce interfacial thermal resistance.
The chemical and microstructural complexity of the W–Ta–Cr–V–Hf HEA mitigates irradiation-induced defect accumulation.
The HEA-coated W–Cu composite will have approximately 10–20% higher effective thermal conductivity than an otherwise comparable uncoated W–Cu composite.
The proposed benefit should persist under high temperature, thermal cycling, and neutron or ion irradiation representative of fusion-reactor joints.
The predicted improvement is conditional on the HEA interlayer remaining chemically stable and nanocrystalline during high-temperature irradiation service.
The W–Ta–Cr–V–Hf coating material can retain a single-phase microstructure and irradiation-resistant grain structure at elevated temperature.
